verses.author: model_A
verses.text: A boat leaves the harbor before anyone is awake to see it go.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
Someone left the porch light on anyway,
not knowing for what,
just in case something needed finding its way back.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
Fog erases the road behind the mail truck,
the driver hums a song with no ending,
delivers what the morning hasn't asked for yet.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
Someone finally throws out the calendar from two years back,
tapes the new one up crooked,
already circling a date that hasn't happened yet.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
The dog waits by the door for no one in particular,
tail going still when the wind moves the trees,
mistaking almost anything for arrival.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
A kettle forgets it was ever filled,
whistles anyway,
steam finding the window someone left cracked for no reason.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
The neighbor's porch light burns through breakfast,
left on since some forgotten dusk,
insisting the dark already left.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
Someone else's mail keeps arriving,
a name half-familiar in the slot,
and still we hold it like it might be ours to open.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
The calendar still shows last month,
a red circle around a day already spent,
and no one's reached to turn the page.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
The dog waits at the door for a walk
that isn't coming,
tail still going, hope not yet caught up to the hour.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
The kettle clicks off unheard,
steam thinning into the ceiling light,
some small readiness going to waste.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
Someone laughs in the next yard,
a sound with no story attached,
and we borrow it anyway, just for the warmth.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
Streetlight flickers on early,
uncertain of the hour itself,
committing anyway.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
My phone buzzes with someone else's good news,
and I feel the small tug
of wanting it to be mine.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
The cat stretches once, decides against it,
folds back into the same warm circle
of sun that hasn't moved in an hour.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
Steam rises off the kettle
into nothing, into everything,
and still I wait for it to say something.
